style: Resilient, transition-focused side under Sebastien Migne built on a deep, compact defensive block and quick counters rather than sustained build-up. Squad drawn almost entirely from a France- and Belgium-developed diaspora.
recent_form: Reached the World Cup for the first time since 1974, ending a 52-year drought via CONCACAF qualifying. Drawn into a brutal Group C with Brazil, Morocco and Scotland.

key_players.name: Wilson Isidor
key_players.note: Sunderland forward and main attacking focal point; switched allegiance from France and made an immediate impact, described as among the best players Haiti have produced.

key_players.name: Jean-Ricner Bellegarde
key_players.note: Wolverhampton Wanderers midfielder and Premier League regular since moving from Strasbourg; key quality switch from France.

key_players.name: Duckens Nazon
key_players.note: Les Grenadiers' all-time leading scorer with 44 goals in 74 caps; experienced finisher.

key_players.name: Johny Placide
key_players.note: Experienced keeper and a key figure behind Haiti's defensive structure.

historical_news: First World Cup appearance since 1974, ending a 52-year wait for Les Grenadiers.
Among the lowest-ranked teams in the field per the 11 June 2026 FIFA ranking.
Diaspora-built squad (only Woodensky Pierre plays his football in Haiti), with several players switching from France for this campaign.
Face a daunting Group C against Brazil, Morocco and Scotland.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Emotional coverage of a historic return after five decades and the rise of a diaspora-led squad, balanced against the toughest of group draws.
